extracted.intended_audience: researchers and authors preparing to submit manuscripts to Royal Society journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting research manuscripts to the Royal Society’s journal portfolio, including scope, ethical, formatting, peer-review and open-access policies. Useful for authors deciding which Royal Society journal to submit to and how to comply with publisher policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match to journal aims and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Please review details about each journal and its aims and scope to verify that your article is a good match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should check the individual journal pages and aims & scope before submitting to ensure topical fit; this is presented as a basic precondition for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good standard of English
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions require a good standard of English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should be written to a good standard of English prior to submission; authors may need to edit or seek language help to meet this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfy ethical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to review our ethical requirements to ensure these are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must ensure their submission meets the publisher's ethical policies (e.g., research ethics approval, authorship, conflicts of interest, data integrity); detailed requirements are provided in the author guidelines and checklists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format-free initial submission
rubrics_metrics.description: We offer format-free initial submission for most of our journals, so you don’t need to worry about reformatting to our reference style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may submit in most reasonable formats for the initial submission and do not need to convert to the journal’s final reference/formatting style at first; follow any further instructions in the author guidelines for revised/final submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model (anonymity and type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most Royal Society journals are normally peer reviewed in a single-anonymized fashion (author names are not concealed, but referee names are), while Notes and Records and Proceedings B are double-anonymized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should check the specific journal’s peer-review model because some journals use double-anonymized review; knowing the model can affect how authors prepare manuscripts (e.g., removing identifying information for double-anonymized review).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of peer review information / transparent peer review options
rubrics_metrics.description: For Royal Society Open Science, Open Biology and Proceedings B, publication of peer review information (anonymous by default unless the reviewer signs their report) is mandatory. For Proceedings A and Biology Letters, we offer authors the option to publish peer review information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware whether the journal mandates or offers optional publication of peer review reports and what anonymity defaults apply; check journal policy if you have concerns about revealing peer review history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with funder mandates (e.g., Plan S)
rubrics_metrics.description: All our journals are compliant with funder mandates such as Plan S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors subject to funder open access mandates can publish with Royal Society journals while meeting those mandates; check specific OA routes and requirements (licence types, embargoes) in the journal’s policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access publication options and discounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Open access publishing including APC-free open access publication through Read & Publish, Subscribe to Open and our Royal Society Open Access Equity scheme. Authors at institutions with OA Membership receive a 25% discount on OA publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should review available open-access routes (including APC-free agreements and discount schemes) and select the option that meets funder/institutional requirements; eligibility depends on institutional agreements and schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality copy-editing and production standards
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publisher will provide professional copy-editing and production services for accepted papers; authors should still ensure clarity and correctness in submitted manuscripts to ease production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit of supplementary material (Figshare)
rubrics_metrics.description: Free deposit of supplementary material (including video) in Figshare; all are fully citable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can deposit supplementary datasets, code, and multimedia in Figshare free of charge, which aids reproducibility and citation; follow the journal’s instructions for linking or submitting supplementary items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ease of submission and transfer options
rubrics_metrics.description: Ease of submission and author care: either directly to us or for some journals via BioRxiv Transfers to Royal Society Open Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may submit directly or use transfer services (e.g., from bioRxiv) where supported; check whether your chosen journal accepts transfers and the process involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to open science and open data
rubrics_metrics.description: A commitment to open science, open data and optional transparent peer review on some journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged (and in some cases required) to make data and code openly available according to journal/data policies; consult the author guidelines for data availability statement requirements and acceptable repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and inclusion in submissions and editorial processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society’s journals aim to foster inclusive science ... Submissions are encouraged and welcomed from all authors, regardless of their characteristics, protected or otherwise. We are committed to equal opportunity and work diligently to mitigate bias in our editorial review processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors from any background are encouraged to submit; the publisher states active efforts to reduce bias in editorial decisions and to implement good practices for inclusive scientific publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional support for early career researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional support and guidance for early career researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early career authors can access specific resources and guidance (ECR resource hub) about the publishing process; consult the publisher’s resources for mentorship and practical help preparing submissions.
